title: The Chant That Was Too Long

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE I: SONGS, CHANTS, SPEECHES AND WELCOMES (LCA-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola sings, chants and speaks for itself: welcoming a new leader, wishing travelers luck, greeting newcomers and newborns, rallying for hard work, standing up for each other, and arguing about who gets the next verse.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: An elder insists on the full blessing chant before every meal, and it takes forever: shorten it, or keep it as it is.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) believes the old blessing chant must be said in full before every meal. The full chant has eighty-one lines. The food is always cold by the end. (friend) has started bringing a snack to eat during the chant, and the other children want to know where (friend.he/she) got it. What should the village do?

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a catch, fruit); the village's stores do not change -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The village asks (subject) to pick the most important lines. (subject) is deeply unhappy about this and takes three days to choose. The new chant has twelve lines. The food is warm. On festival days, (subject) still says all eighty-one, and everyone politely waits.

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a catch, fruit); the village's stores do not change -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village keeps the full chant. (friend) and the children learn all eighty-one lines, mostly so they can say them faster. Before long, meals start with a chant at astonishing speed, led by six children and one baffled elder.
